result:
I've written the plan for w216 (supervision r154–r157) to `.shop/scratch/2-plan/plan.md`, and the result file is marked `DONE` with no questions.

All ten accepted scenarios are red today because their first step has no step definition. Behind those steps, there is no code yet for any of the four requirements.

**What the plan has `work run` do before a branch review:**
- **Runs (r154):** after the push check passes, it makes all the runs at the head commit in the review's own worktree, then writes the brief, then starts the reviewer. The runs are the whole suite, each work-item's scenarios, each work-item's `check:`, `tools check --base <Base>`, `tools size`, `features deprecated` and `features bindings`.
- **Run results (r155):** the brief gives each run's command, exit code and full output, plus the commit they ran at. The output is indented so that `Head:` stays the only line the existing code reads as the reviewed head.
- **Commits (r156):** each commit is attributed to a work-item if it was in that item's recorded merge or is one of its `work: <item> …` status-change commits. Every other commit is given as "none". The brief also gives the diff from base to head without `.shop/`.
- **Files to read (r157):** a `Read:` list with each capability the work-items are under, the design-decisions those capabilities rest on (by id), and each work-item's plan, report and findings files.
- **Reviewer prompt:** `agents/bdd-branch-reviewer.md` changes so the reviewer reads all this from the brief instead of re-running or re-deriving it.

**How I settled the researcher's three open conflicts:**
- **Commit attribution:** I used the recorded merges. The other reading, which takes every commit between an item's status changes, would wrongly give the concurrent `notes.txt` commit to w1, and the r156 scenario says it belongs to none.
- **Whole suite:** I used the existing suite command naming one of the initiative's work-items. At review time all of them are green or withdrawn, so failures already expected elsewhere are counted the same way as at a merge. A bare run would instead show other initiatives' parked scenarios (w212's) as failures.
- **`tools check`:** run with `--base <Base>`, matching the base-to-head range in r156.

**Tests broken:** none. I checked each existing test the research listed against these choices; no new log line is added and the `Head:` reading is unchanged. Every existing scenario that reaches a branch review will now also make these runs in its fixture repository, so the suite will get slower.

**File set:** `scripts/supervise_review.py`, two new modules (`scripts/supervise_branch_runs.py`, `scripts/supervise_review_read.py`), `agents/bdd-branch-reviewer.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and three test files: the new step module `tests/scenarios/supervision_branch_steps.py`, `test_supervision.py` and `supervision_world.py`. I dropped four files the researcher listed because no decision changes them: `supervise.py`, `supervise_merge.py`, `supervise_worker.py` and `supervision_given.py`.

**Open cases left for the implementer:** a run that can't start, very long output, an initiative with no base, a `check:` that needs a shell or has quoting the frontmatter reader changes, and a project size limit other than 300. `tools check` may also come back red at head in this repository because of ruff errors already in the ledger; under r155 that is reported, not hidden.
